messages:
Incident Bot: PAGING eng-oncall: spike of 5xx errors on /v1/generate (service=api-gateway, upstream=upstream-provider-x). Current 5m error rate=12%. Severity=page.
Alex: On it — pulling graphs.
Priya: I see the spike started ~2999991180 (09:12 UTC). Upstream timeouts and 502s dominate.
Jamie: Is there a recent deploy? I don't see a rollout in the last 2 hours.
Priya: No deploy. Traces show increased RTT to upstream-provider-x at the TCP level.
Alex: Mitigation plan: 1) divert traffic for heavy routes to fallback pool (model-pool-b). 2) bump proxy retry/backoff conservative. 3) suppress noisy pager for 5-10% if upstream tagged. I'll start 1 and 2 now.
Jamie: Please add a short TTL on the traffic split (10m) so we can revert if it hurts latency.
Alex: Doing this: `kubectl patch svc api-gateway -p '{"spec":{"trafficPolicy":{"split":{"model-pool-a":0.0,"model-pool-b":1.0}}}}'` — applied.
Priya: Proxy retry increased: `gateway.conf -> upstream.retry=3, upstream.retry_backoff_ms=200` — reloaded.
Sasha: Quick ask about alerts: current pager fires on global 5xx > 3% for 5m. This is noisy for upstream blips. Suggest: create two-tier alerts: pager only if 5xx > 8% AND customer-impacting routes affected; non-pager for 3-8%. Also tag alerts by upstream so we can silence per-upstream without cluster-wide suppression.
Nikhil: Agreed. We can tighten noise by adding a query like: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (route,upstream) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[5m])) by (route,upstream)` then alert on that per-route-per-upstream.
Alex: For now I've created a temporary mute for upstream=upstream-provider-x for the global pager channel and pushed a non-pager alert to #eng-sre. Mute expires in 30m.
Ops Bot: Mute applied to pager channel for upstream-provider-x until 2999993012.
Jamie: Traffic is stable after split, 5xx down to 2.5% cluster-wide, downstream latency +10ms on fallback pool but acceptable.
Priya: Confirmed reduced errors on customer-facing routes. No active customer pages.
Sasha: Follow-ups: 1) Create a dedicated dashboard panel for per-upstream error-rate + latency. 2) Update alert definitions to be per-upstream and add severity mapping (pager at >8% OR >4% for SLO-critical routes). 3) Add runbook steps for muting single-upstream without global pager mute.
Alex: I'll hand off to Jamie for the 10:00 UTC on-call rotation. Jamie — you own creating the ticket and the dashboard tiles.
Jamie: Taking handoff. I'll open INFR-342 (alerting/dashboard) and a short post-incident note.
Nikhil: For the dashboard query examples, I'll drop a Grafana panel JSON in the ticket.
Alex: Thanks all :thumbsup:. Leaving the temporary traffic split in place until Jamie confirms dashboard + alert changes.
Jamie: Will revert traffic split if we see regression. Handoff complete.
Incident Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (status=mitigated). No customer pages.
Sasha: Post-mortem action items assigned in INFR-342: update alerts, add per-upstream panels, and add upstream health probe to reduce false positives.
Jamie: Filing the follow-up now and tagging owners.
Ops Bot: Reminder scheduled: runbook review in 48h.
